causes: Count I — Fourteenth Amendment Procedural Due Process, Structural Bias (§ 1983; against Candelaria, individual capacity) — DMV's dual investigator/advocate/adjudicator role, condemned in Cal. DUI Lawyers Ass'n v. DMV, Knudsen v. DMV, and Clarke v. Gordon

Count II — Fourteenth Amendment Procedural Due Process, Denial of a Fair Hearing (§ 1983; against Candelaria, individual capacity) — ratified the fabricated DS-367 without engaging the Detention Certificate, dashcam evidence, or Mercer v. DMV

Count III — Fourteenth Amendment Procedural Due Process, Clear Absence of Statutory Jurisdiction (§ 1983; against Candelaria, individual capacity) — Stump v. Sparkman; APS refusal framework's 'lawfully arrested' predicate (Veh. Code § 13353(a)(1)) destroyed by the § 851.6 Detention Certificate before the hearing

Count IV — Declaratory Relief (§ 1983; 28 U.S.C. §§ 2201, 2202; against Gordon, official capacity, Ex parte Young) — DMV's dual-role APS framework and its treatment of the Detention Certificate violate the Fourteenth Amendment

Count V — Injunctive Relief (§ 1983; against Gordon, official capacity, Ex parte Young) — vacatur of the suspension, the $125 reissue fee, and the three-year SR-22 mandate; structural reform of the APS hearing process
key_facts: Companion action to Matter 7 (same Feb. 11, 2025 APS Decision, APS Case No. 34739340, suspending Plaintiff's Class A CDL for one year), refiled in the N.D. Cal. under the Ngwa Nforbi name form rather than the Newanforbi caption Matter 7 uses. Candelaria, a DMV Driver Safety Hearing Officer, presided over the January 24, 2025 Microsoft Teams APS hearing and issued the February 11, 2025 written decision sustaining the suspension, the $125 reissue fee, and a three-year SR-22 requirement running through approximately February 2028. The decision rested on the same DS-367 and CHP Arrest-Investigation Report (CHP Case No. RJ68845) pleaded as fabricated in the companion Ngwa Nforbi v. Meza-Gonzalez & Melano action (Matter 32) — Candelaria's decision never engages the CHP's own November 5, 2024 Penal Code § 851.6 Detention Certificate reclassifying the encounter as 'a detention only, not an arrest.' Gordon, DMV Director, is sued only in his official capacity for prospective relief; Clarke v. Gordon, 104 Cal.App.5th 1267 (2024), named him personally four months before this hearing.
procedural_status: On August 7, 2026 a Complaint for Damages and for Declaratory and Injunctive Relief under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, 28 U.S.C. §§ 2201-2202, and Ex parte Young was drafted under the Ngwa Nforbi v. Candelaria & Gordon caption for the Northern District of California, together with the supporting intake packet: JS 44 civil cover sheet (nature of suit 440, federal question, jury demand, related case 4:26-cv-05953-ASK), AO 440 summonses for Candelaria and Gordon (service at the DMV's Legal Affairs Division, Sacramento headquarters — the complaint gives no office address for Candelaria, whose hearing was conducted remotely), and a Consent to Magistrate Judge Jurisdiction form (CONSENT checked). Nothing has been filed: no case number has issued, the civil action number and clerk signature blocks on both summonses are blank, the JS 44 and consent form signature lines are blank for Plaintiff's wet signature, and the consent form's case-number field is blank pending assignment (due within 14 days of case initiation).
damages: Prayer against Candelaria: compensatory damages not less than $150,000 (lost wages, lost employment, the $125 reissue fee, SR-22 premiums paid and continuing, out-of-pocket and reputational/emotional-distress damages) and punitive damages not less than $100,000 — a $250,000 floor used on the JS 44 demand line. Against Gordon: declaratory judgment and injunctive relief only (vacatur of the suspension, the reissue fee, and the SR-22 mandate; structural reform), no damages. These figures overlap the CDL-suspension damages already pleaded in Matter 7 for the same underlying decision; do not aggregate the two without reconciling.
risk: Same core risk as Matter 32: this is a second N.D. Cal. filing over facts already pending in Matter 7 (E.D. Cal., F&R stage) and referenced in the Serrato action (4:26-cv-05953-ASK) and the Meza-Gonzalez complaint (Matter 32) — filing here while Matter 7 remains live invites claim-splitting and issue-preclusion arguments from the AG, and a Civil L.R. 3-12 relation motion to the Serrato docket should accompany any filing. Quasi-judicial immunity is the central substantive risk for Candelaria: the complaint pleads investigative/advocacy conduct and a clear-absence-of-jurisdiction theory under Stump v. Sparkman specifically to defeat it, but that is a live, contested question, not a settled one. Eleventh Amendment immunity is pled around via Ex parte Young for Gordon (official capacity, prospective relief only) — do not add damages against Gordon.
